messages:
Noah: quick heads-up — just merged CascadeHealth adapter (cascade/adapter-2026-01) into staging. Ran qpack (cascade-onboard-qpack, 300 QA prompts) — int4 path shows a quality drop.
Mika: paste the quickpack metrics? which baseline did you compare against?
Noah: baseline redwood/gptj-13b:v2026-01 (fp16). Quickpack: cascade-onboard-qpack (300 prompts). Results:
- fp16 baseline accuracy: 82.0%
- int4 after merge: 77.1%  (drop -4.9 pts)
- PPL: baseline 13.0 -> 16.2
Mika: yikes. any large diffs or tokenization warnings?
Noah: got a tokenizer warning during the merge step: `WARNING: tokenizer vocab mismatch — adapter(50299) vs base(50288) — delta=11`
Amy: if the adapter brought new tokens we should either align tokenizers during merge or do a controlled vocab expansion with product/solutions consent.
Eli: also saw a local runtime KV warning: `KVCache: expected seq_len 64 got 65` — could indicate kv-cache alignment issues after quantization.
Noah: sample idx 88 repro:
```
PROMPT: "Who leads CascadeHealth?"
BASE: "Cascade Health is led by Dr. Lina Torres."
ADAPTER(int4): "CascadeHealth was founded in 2016."  <-- dropped the leader name
```
Jen: can you upload the failing examples and the exact merge/quant commands to artifacts? I'll spin a canary in dedicated pool and run the triage steps. ETA ~45m.
Noah: uploaded failures to staging artifacts: https://staging.internal/redwood/artifacts/cas-fails-2009876543.json
CI-bot: adapters/eval/cascade cascade-onboard-qpack (int4) — 5 failed of 300 — see artifacts link. Perf: latency +7ms/token vs baseline, memory stable.
Mika: proposed triage plan: 1) run `tools/tokenizer_diff.py` to enumerate adapter tokens; 2) if delta <= 12, rerun merge with `--align-tokenizer` and re-quant; 3) if delta > 20, escalate to solutions-eng for vocab policy and customer sign-off. Also compare per-channel int4 vs symmetric int4 quant configs.
Noah: merge command I used: `python infra/merge_lora.py --base redwood/gptj-13b --adapter cascade/adapter-2026-01 --out staging/cascade-merged`
Noah: quant command used: `rw-quantize --model staging/cascade-merged --mode int4 --per-channel --calib-samples 512 --out staging/cascade-merged-int4`
Mika: running tokenizer_diff now. If tokens are mostly short medical abbreviations and <= 10, align-merge should be straightforward.
Mika: tokenizer diff summary: adapter introduces 9 tokens (mostly medical shortforms). Mapping looks straightforward. Kicking off align-merge + re-quant + quickpack.
CI-bot: adapters/merge/cascade — merge completed with align-tokenizer. artifacts: staging/cascade-merged-aligned.tar.gz
CI-bot: adapters/eval/cascade cascade-onboard-qpack (int4 aligned) — 300 tests run — failures 0 — accuracy 81.8% — PPL 13.1 :tada:
Noah: great. Note for runbook: prefer align-tokenizer merge when adapter_vocab_delta <= 10. For deltas > 20, require product/solutions review for controlled vocab expansion.
Jen: I'll update onboarding checklist and add a small patch to merge_lora.py to default to `--align-tokenizer` when adapter_vocab_delta <= 10, plus a short note about KVCache sanity checks.
Noah: thanks all, closing triage. :white_check_mark:
